summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and chronic obstructive lung disease, was admitted for hypoxemia and increased oxygen requirements, found to have multifocal pneumonia on chest imaging. She had recently completed treatment for a UTI and reported a history of aspiration. Despite being afebrile and without leukocytosis, she required up to 12 liters of oxygen initially. Treatment with vancomycin and Zosyn was initiated due to prior MRSA and aspiration risk. She responded well, weaning to her baseline 2 liters within two days. Urine culture showed no growth, and Legionella antigen was negative. She remained stable, with plans for completion of an 8-day IV antibiotic course at home via PICC line. Discharge was arranged with home health support and follow-up with primary and pulmonary care.
